name: Fintan
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fintan was an ancient invader who could change form, and one of his shapes was the eagle. In British legend the magical pig Henwen brought forth eaglets, bees, and wolves. The hero Lleu Llaw Gyffes of Wales entered the eagle's form after his wife killed him. The bird was tied to oracles, and its arrival could be read as a sign of what lay ahead. A shape-shifting magician or a bard might wear the eagle's shape. In Welsh folklore the eagles of Mount Snowdon were oracular and could manage the weather. People were thought to gain psychic powers if their forebears had dined on eagle, and that gift reached the ninth generation.

okr.objective: Fintan is an ancient shape-shifter who took the form of an eagle.
